channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco's open-source Shirudo runtime lets teams keep running Linux systems protected while patches roll out, and in controlled tests a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell attack on Elasticsearch without a reboot. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Codex CLI 0.172.0
item.description: Codex CLI 0.172.0 is out with a full rust-v0.171.0...rust-v0.172.0 changelog and GitHub release page, plus the 0.170.0-to-0.171.0 update record for tracking ChatGPT and Codex changes. (OpenAI Codex Changelog)

item.title: RoboTrack: Point tracking for real-world robotic manipulation
item.description: Ai2's RoboTrack benchmark and data suite includes 307 human-annotated videos from DROID and shows leading point trackers score far below existing benchmarks on real robotic manipulation, while its RoboTracker-Warp reaches state-of-the-art on four of five evaluations. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Issue statuses and repository boards are in public preview
item.description: GitHub issues now get finer statuses beyond open/closed in public preview, repository boards with status: filtering, and GraphQL, REST API and MCP server read/write access, with Copilot automation triggering status changes. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: A more tailored Google Search that’s uniquely yours
item.description: Google Search's Personal Intelligence lets users opt in to connect Google Wallet, Drive, and Gemini so AI Mode answers draw on spending, documents, and chats, with Wallet rolling out today and Drive/Gemini in coming weeks, adjustable in settings. (Google AI Blog)

item.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
item.description: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI used Gemini 4 agent teams plus Lean formal verification to generate more efficient quantum circuits for fusion energy, chemistry and enzyme simulations, then open-sourced the results. (Google DeepMind)

item.title: Secret scanning reduces false positives for Slack
item.description: GitHub’s secret scanning now cuts false-positive detections for Slack secrets, with its slack_incoming_webhook_url detector excluding certain URLs to reduce mismatches and spare developers unnecessary invalid alerts. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Richpanel helps companies automate 50% of support in 30 days
item.description: Richpanel's Boss AI uses GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol to write procedures and call tools for support agents, with GPT-6 Luna handling conversations; after about 300 deployments in six months, it promises 50% support automation in 30 days or refund. (OpenAI News)

item.title: AI now takes over code merges too: Anthropic launches Claude Ship
item.description: Anthropic's Claude Ship beta, reported November 23 by TechCrunch, gives AI agents code review—now generally available—plus a PR Steward that fixes failed CI and merge conflicts and Claude Approvals that enforces natural-language policies. (AIbase)

item.title: Code coverage uploads now flag invalid report formats
item.description: GitHub Code Quality’s upload-code-coverage action now rejects non-Cobertura XML reports, failing the upload with “This file is not a Cobertura XML report” in the Actions log instead of appearing successful while leaving pull requests without coverage. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Connected intelligence for in-house legal
item.description: OpenAI’s Stacey Wang and Craig Bruney join LECG’s Mary O’Carroll and Cooley’s Richard Segal to discuss how AI helps in-house legal teams connect business context, build reusable workflows, and get more from outside counsel. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship beta: code review, fixes, and approvals — AI handles the whole pipeline
item.description: Anthropic's Claude Ship beta splits merge work across three agents: Code Review, already generally available, handles review, PR Steward clears CI failures and merge conflicts with per-change undo notes, and Claude Approvals enforces repo-specific natural-language policies. (AIbase)

item.title: Usage reports will include a user ID column starting December 1
item.description: Starting December 1, 2026, GitHub's detailed, AI and premium request usage reports add a user_id column beside username, shifting later columns right and requiring position-based scripts to switch to header-based parsing. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: GPT-6.2 Sol rolls out across all of ChatGPT: it can read stop signs clearly — and will proactively remind you it's time to cut prices
item.description: GPT-6.2 Sol landed on ChatGPT on November 24, able to read the tiny symbols on parking signs and proactively flag when a product's price drops, while some GPT-5.6 models retire December 23. (AIbase)

item.title: OpenAI teams up with Cisco to open-source Shirudo, giving AI agent systems a "round-the-clock bulletproof vest
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco open-sourced Shirudo on November 24, a Linux runtime environment where AI agents write dynamic eBPF rules to shield vulnerable systems without kernel changes or restarts, buying security teams time to test and deploy patches. (AIbase)

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
item.description: Anthropic's Claude Ship lets AI agents review, fix and approve code changes, taking over routine approvals to clear the bottleneck created as AI-generated code piles up. (TechCrunch AI)

item.title: One Prompt, One "Disaster": Ministry of Public Security Cybersecurity Bureau Names 10 Typical AI Disinformation Cases
item.description: China's Ministry of Public Security cyber-security bureau published 10 typical AI rumor cases on November 24, including Ma's AI-generated video of the Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon glass bridge collapsing and Wu's fabricated Guangzhou Huadu night market flood, with 3 cases leading to criminal coercive measures and 7 to administrative penalties. (AIbase)

item.title: Cashed Out Before the Stock Took Off: Anthropic CEO Sells $280 Million on IPO Day
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sold 3,378,378 shares at the $83 IPO price on listing day, cashing out roughly $280.4 million before any post-debut rally, according to a Form 4 filed with the SEC. (AIbase)

item.title: Othor AI — Your Head of Intelligence. Know what your numbers are hiding
item.description: A CAPTCHA "confirm you are not a robot" check blocks the body of Othor AI's page, leaving readers only the title and tagline "Your Head of Intelligence. Know what your numbers are hiding. (Product Hunt)

item.title: Patches take weeks; protection can go live tonight: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco open-sourced Shirudo on November 23, a Linux eBPF-based shield that adds temporary protection without rebooting and, in testing, a Codex-generated layer blocked a Java4Shell attack on Elasticsearch. (AIbase)
